summary: node1 now has an ext4 logical volume mounted at /srv/data. It was grown online from 1 GiB to 2.25 GiB without changing the mount identity or corrupting its contents. Persistent activation and mounting were verified through a full node restart.
actions_performed: Created a persistent 3 GiB loop-backed LVM physical volume, vg_data, and lv_data.
Created and checksummed integrity test files.
Extended the mounted LV and filesystem online from 1 GiB to 2.25 GiB.
Configured Alpine startup to restore the loop device, activate the VG, and mount /srv/data.
Safely restarted node1 and verified persistent recovery and write access.

evidence.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data
evidence.summary: Created vg_data/lv_data, formatted it as ext4, mounted it at /srv/data, and populated integrity files.

evidence.requirement: Grow the volume to at least 2 GB while mounted and preserve its contents
evidence.summary: The filesystem was extended online from 1 GiB to 2.25 GiB. Mount ID 36 and device 252:0 remained unchanged, and both SHA-256 checks passed before and after resizing.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 8fc12b71-5b5c-41f4-bf51-798c54ab693a; reboot acknowledgement was captured; the new boot ID was ab4d42ea-7d37-43ac-82f3-f95961fcc11b. After restart, the loop PV, VG, 2.25 GiB LV, /srv/data mount, original checksums, and new write access were all healthy.
